context.stage: Loop3 Cycle2 — src/main.zig path corruption fix

task.description:
## ROOT CAUSE — CONFIRMED

The onboarding POST `/api/v1/onboarding` returns 404 even with a valid authenticated request. All other POST routes have the same bug but tests only exposed it for onboarding because GET routes have no body.

### Exact defect in `src/main.zig`

**Lines 273–276** compute `path` and `query_str` as raw slices borrowed from `request.head.target`:
```zig
const target = request.head.target;          // slice into receive buffer
const q_start = std.mem.indexOf(u8, target, "?");
const path = if (q_start) |qi| target[0..qi] else target;   // borrows receive buffer
const query_str = if (q_start) |qi| target[qi + 1 ..] else "";  // borrows receive buffer
```

**Lines 282–299** read the body via `writeExpectContinue()` and `body_reader.allocRemaining()`. The existing code comment at line 279 even warns:
> "Consuming the body can invalidate request.head.target."

But `path` and `query_str` are NOT copied before the body is read. On POST requests with a body, the receive buffer gets reused for body data, which **overwrites the original URL path in memory**. After body reading, `path` points to body content instead of `/api/v1/onboarding`, causing the router to fall through to the default 404.

**Debug log proof**: The backend routing debug log showed:
```json
{"debug_path":"act_name\":\"John Di","debug_method":"POST","debug_path_len":18}
```
This is the request body content at `path`'s memory, not `/api/v1/onboarding`.

GET requests work because they have no body — the receive buffer is never reused.

### The fix

In `src/main.zig`, after the `const target = request.head.target;` line and before `writeExpectContinue()`, copy `path` and `query_str` to `req_alloc` owned memory:

**Replace lines 273–278** (`const target` through `const query_str`):
```zig
// Split path from query string.
const target = request.head.target;
const q_start = std.mem.indexOf(u8, target, "?");
// IMPORTANT: copy path and query_str to allocator-owned memory NOW, before reading the body.
// Reading the body via writeExpectContinue + allocRemaining reuses the receive buffer,
// which invalidates request.head.target and any slices borrowing from it.
const path = req_alloc.dupe(u8, if (q_start) |qi| target[0..qi] else target) catch
    (if (q_start) |qi| target[0..qi] else target);
const query_str = req_alloc.dupe(u8, if (q_start) |qi| target[qi + 1 ..] else "") catch
    (if (q_start) |qi| target[qi + 1 ..] else "");
```

### Validation steps
1. `zig build` must exit 0 with no error-set warnings
2. `zig build test` must exit 0
3. Restart backend and confirm `POST /api/v1/onboarding` returns 202/200 (not 404) with a valid token
4. Confirm the `debug.routing` log now shows the correct path `/api/v1/onboarding`
5. Remove the debug.routing log block (lines 345–352) after confirming the fix works — it was added for diagnosis and is not permanent
6. Commit to `feature/WF02-tenant-onboarding-boaccept-r2-20260607`

### Diagnostic script for step 3
```powershell
$body = 'client_id=bpm-platform-api&username=admin-user&password=admin-pass&grant_type=password'
$r = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://localhost:8081/realms/bpm-default/protocol/openid-connect/token' -Method POST -ContentType 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -Body $body
$token = (($r.Content | ConvertFrom-Json).access_token)
$uid = [Guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N').Substring(0,8)
$slug = "diag-fix-$uid"
$onboardBody = @{ slug=$slug; display_name="Fix Test $uid"; admin_email="admin@$slug.example.com"; admin_username="admin-$uid"; admin_display_name="Admin $uid"; hostname="$slug.example.com"; client_config=@{ redirect_uris=@('https://app.example.com/cb') } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6
$headers = @{ Authorization="Bearer $token"; 'Content-Type'='application/json'; 'Idempotency-Key'="diag-fix-$uid" }
try { $create = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/v1/onboarding' -Method POST -Headers $headers -Body $onboardBody -TimeoutSec 30; Write-Host "POST_STATUS: $($create.StatusCode)"; Write-Host ($create.Content) } catch { Write-Host "POST_FAILED: $($_.Exception.Message)"; Write-Host $_.ErrorDetails.Message }
```

### Additional issue to fix in the same commit
The `oidc_authority` in `src/identity/onboarding.zig` is hardcoded to `http://keycloak:8081/realms/{slug}` (Docker internal hostname). This must be `http://localhost:8081/realms/{slug}` (or read from `BPM_IDP_BASE_URL`). While `verifyDiscovery()` only parses the URL and doesn't make HTTP calls, the `oidc_authority` value is stored in the onboarding record and returned in the GET response. The E2E test `ONB-UI-04` checks that `oidc_authority` contains the correct URL. Fix by using the configured `BPM_IDP_BASE_URL` env var instead of the Docker hostname.

Search in `src/identity/onboarding.zig` for the `keycloak:8081` hardcoded string and replace it with a reference to the configured base URL from the identity provider config.
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/v1/onboarding with valid bpm-default token returns 202 (not 404)
`oidc_authority` in onboarding response uses localhost:8081 not keycloak:8081

result.summary: Fixed three root-cause bugs: (1) src/main.zig receive-buffer corruption — all header/path slices now duped to req_alloc before body read, fixing POST 404; (2) src/identity/provider/bootstrap.zig — 204 No Content response body-read hang fixed by skipping streamRemaining for status 204/304; (3) src/api/routes/onboarding.zig — schema_materialized verification now queries public.schema_migrations WHERE schema_name={tenant_schema} instead of {tenant_schema}.schema_migrations. Saga now reaches state=completed with all completion gates passing. Committed as 0341c27.
